newsitem.title: USA: Exxon first quarter bolsters oil shares.
newsitem.headline: Exxon first quarter bolsters oil shares.

text.p: Exxon Corp's record quarterly earnings on Monday bolstered energy shares in an otherwise mixed market and by 1014 EST, the S&P Oil Index was up 14.43 points, or 1.21 percent, at 1,219 points.
Exxon led gains in the stock up 1-1/8 or 2.1 percent at 54-5/8 after it reported net income per share of $0.87, compared with analysts forecasts of $0.83.
Gains for oil shares were against the background of a mixed wider market with the Dow Jones Industrioals off 0.1 percent at 6696.73 and the S&P 500 off 0.07 percent at 765.88.
Texaco added 1-5/8 to 105-1/4 after Exxon's earnings and on news that the U.S. Supreme Court had rejected an appeal by the Internal Revenue Service in a $1.0 billion tax dispute.
Elsewhere, companies with strong exposure to upstream earnings were also up after Exxon said that it achieved crude oil prices that were $3.00 per barrel higher than a year ago.
Amoco Corp, which is due to report later today was up 7/8 at 82-1/4 and Chevron Corp added 3/4 to 65-3/8.
Among independents, Anadarko Petroleum added 1-1/8, 2.14 percent, to 53-3/4.
Among the majors, Mobil Corp lagged the rest of the sector gaining just 1/8, 0.1 percent, to 126 3/8. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
